label: Comparatives
outcome: Lo studente confronta due persone, oggetti, luoghi o situazioni scegliendo la forma comparativa appropriata e completando il confronto con than quando necessario, senza costruzioni doppie come more cheaper.
must_master: selected short CVC adjectives with doubled final consonant
than after a comparative when the second term is expressed
choose the comparative form from meaning in a clear two-item comparison

scope_boundary.superlatives: Do not teach superlatives systematically here. They belong to the separate superlatives Recovery topic.
scope_boundary.equality: Do not make as...as a core target in this version; the curriculum marks equality as programme-dependent.
scope_boundary.advanced_modifiers: Do not teach far/much/a bit + comparative, less than, or double comparatives.
scope_boundary.lexis: Use familiar A1+/A2 adjectives; difficulty must come from the comparison decision, not rare vocabulary.

italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: This bag is more cheaper than that one.
italian_learner_risks.target: This bag is cheaper than that one.

italian_learner_risks.risk: using more with a short adjective instead of the regular -er pattern
italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: My room is more small than yours.
italian_learner_risks.target: My room is smaller than yours.

italian_learner_risks.risk: forgetting consonant doubling in common short CVC adjectives

italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: Today is more good than yesterday.
The bus is slower then the train.
italian_learner_risks.target: The bus is slower than the train.

context_bank: comparing two phones before buying one
choosing between two routes to school
comparing prices and sizes in a shop
comparing two timetables or travel options

requirements: explain the two main form families before spelling detail
show -er, -ier, doubled consonant, more, better/worse and than
explicitly reject double comparative forms such as more cheaper
six scaffolded graded checks after teaching
include one short controlled production item
mix form choice, spelling, irregular forms and meaningful comparison
include a connected dialogue or decision context
include at least one Italian-to-English translation
increase autonomy from selection to production
approximately 60 percent standard and 40 percent challenge

quality_rejections: ten near-identical prompts asking only for -er or more
distractors that are impossible English rather than plausible learner errors
a task where the title states which comparative form to use
mixing superlatives into the assessed target
treating adjective length as a perfect mechanical rule with no taught exceptions
using than when no second term of comparison is expressed
ambiguous contexts where no comparison between two entities is established
translations with only one accepted word order when more than one natural form is valid
